summary: Same theme (blue rain + white lightning flashes) and an identical, fully-live 4-slider surface, but the rain body is drawn completely differently — the port renders a fine periodic texture of horizontal dashes over a permanent dim haze instead of sparse long vertical/diagonal streaks on black — and it falls ~4.5x too slow at half the peak brightness while lightning strikes ~3-4x too often.
observations: Both sides compile and run clean on the default 16x16 grid rig (256 px); no compileError/runtimeError, wantsSensors=false on both, no runs produced harness warnings. Neither side dies: over a 120 s window (light-0.5) and an 8 s late window at --skip 120 both are still animating (zeroMotionFrames 1/600 and 1/160 respectively, brightnessTrend volatile on both). Steady state is not the problem.

Control surface MATCHES exactly: both sides expose sliderSpeed (Speed), sliderAngle (Angle), sliderScale (Scale), sliderLightning (Lightning), all kind=slider. --probe-controls reports all four responsive on both sides (orig maxDeltaLit 12.9-19.5; port 14.3-26.8).

RAIN GLYPH IS THE HEADLINE DIVERGENCE. At untouched defaults on a 48x48 grid (label untouched48) the original draws 2-3 long, thick blue streaks slanting ~45deg across the whole canvas on pure black; the port draws stacked HORIZONTAL dashes (~5-8 px wide, ~2 px tall) in a few fixed near-vertical columns plus faint arc-shaped haze. Same divergence on the default 16x16 rig: orig = 1-px-wide streaks with a bright head and a fading tail; port = 2-px-wide horizontal 'OO' segments.

SPATIAL FREQUENCY along the fall axis (row-profile DFT, 48x48, angle=0, lightning=0, label vel48): original's dominant component is k=1 (magnitude 3339, next 956 at k=2) — one or two long features per canvas height. Port's dominant components are k=7/6/5 (1722/1592/1027) — a repeating texture roughly every 7 px of a 48-px canvas. The port's 'rain' is a periodic stripe texture, not discrete drops.

PORT'S DROPS SIT IN FIXED COLUMNS. With lightning=0 over 120 s (label light-0), the port's per-column-mean rhythm image is a set of perfectly static vertical bands; column-profile cross-correlation between frames 0.05-0.30 s apart gives dx=0 at c=0.97-0.999 (label dump3). Its 16-px column profile is 0.5 0.3 0.4 0.4 11.0 11.1 1.3 1.3 0.4 1.3 1.3 2.6 3.9 7.2 6.5 6.6 — columns 4/5 are always bright, 0-3 always near-dark. The original's column profile drifts steadily (dx -1,-2,-3,-4,-5 over 0.05..0.25 s) and its rhythm image is an even wash.

PIXEL DENSITY / BACKGROUND: at lightning=0 on the default rig (label vel16) the original lights 39% of pixels (27% above value 8) with true 0,0,0 elsewhere; the port lights 69% (45% above 8) — it never returns to black, leaving a permanent dim blue haze. At untouched defaults the same gap is 30-37% (orig) vs 69-78% (port).

DROP BRIGHTNESS AND HUE: original drop head peaks at [12,12,254] — pure blue, R exactly == G, saturating to 254. Port drop head peaks at [20,26,161] — only ~63% as bright and cyan-tinted (G > R by ~30%). Over a 60 s survey the port's meanR/meanG run 10.8/11.6 against the original's 1.4/1.4, i.e. the port is far less blue-pure overall.

FALL SPEED IS ~4.5x TOO SLOW. Whole-frame 2D cross-correlation at angle=0, lightning=0: original shifts +3 rows per 0.05 s on the 16x16 default rig (60 rows/s = 3.75 canvas-heights/s, label vel16) and ~+38 rows per 0.2 s on 48x48 (~3.9 canvas-heights/s, label ang48-0). The port shifts +4 px per 0.1 s on 48x48 and +0.32 rows/frame at 40 fps on 16x16 — both ~0.83 canvas-heights/s (labels vel48, rain-phase). Ratio ~4.5x. Direction (straight down at angle=0) is correct on both.

Temporal decorrelation confirms the character difference: at sliderSpeed=0.5 the original's frame autocorrelation dips to ~0 by 0.15 s and RECURS to 0.87-0.91 at 0.35-0.40 s (one canvas traverse); the port's recurs at 0.15 s and 0.30 s (its 7-fold texture period). Same underlying velocity ratio.

LIGHTNING RATE IS 3-4x TOO HIGH. 40 s at 20 fps, untouched (label flashscan): original has 6 distinct strikes (t = 5.0/5.55, 12.25, 18.4, 24.85/25.15, 31.45, 37.2/37.5), mean gap ~6.4 s, each strike 1-2 flickers of 0.05-0.10 s. Port has ~17 strikes, mean gap ~2.3 s, several with 4-5 sub-flickers (e.g. 7.95, 8.10, 8.20, 8.35, 8.45). Dialed 120 s runs at 5 fps: sliderLightning=0.5 gives 12 flashes (orig) vs 54 (port); =1.0 gives 23 vs 97. Consistently ~4.3x too frequent at every dial value.

The lightning FLASH ITSELF is a reasonable match: both are a white (R=G=B) radial blob with a soft falloff peaking at 255. The port's is bigger and brighter — at peak the original's frame averages 94.6 with 96% of pixels lit, the port's averages 121.4 with 100% lit, and whole-grid mean brightness maxes at 100 (orig) vs 122 (port).

RESOLUTION BEHAVIOUR: the original is resolution-independent — 8x8, 16x16 and 48x48 all show the same few streaks scaled to the canvas, and its speed in canvas-heights/s is the same at 16x16 and 48x48. The port is also canvas-relative (its ~7-fold texture repeats ~7 times at both 16 and 48 rows), so this axis is not itself a divergence; it just makes the wrong glyph more obvious at 48x48.

Both sides are fps-invariant (time-based, not frame-stepped): measured downward velocity on 48x48 is ~40 px/s for the port at 10, 20 and 40 fps, and the original's is ~170-190 px/s at 10 and 20 fps. No frame-rate-coupling finding.

Both sides are seed-independent: seeds 1, 7 and 1234 give byte-identical stats on both sides (mean 8/motion 7 orig, mean 12/motion 16 port). The pattern is noise/time-driven, not RNG-driven, so no stochastic-character caveat applies.

UNTOUCHED-DEFAULT divergence, reported separately per procedure: untouched, the ORIGINAL's rain falls at a slant (~2 rows down per 1 column left on 16x16, ~45deg on 48x48); the PORT's untouched rain falls straight down. Setting ANY single slider on the original (even sliderLightning=0) snaps its rain to vertical, i.e. the original's untouched slant sits outside what any sliderAngle value reproduces — a setter artefact of the original, noted so a fixer does not chase it.

dials.name: sliderSpeed
dials.origEffect: Continuous fall-rate control. Half-decorrelation time of the frame autocorrelation drops 0.35 s (v=0) -> 0.10 s (v=0.5) -> 0.05 s (v=1); rain visibly accelerates without changing streak shape.
dials.portEffect: Same direction and roughly the same span: half-decorrelation 0.20 s -> 0.05 s -> 0.05 s. Direction correct, but the whole curve is offset because the port's base fall rate is ~4.5x too slow and its finer texture decorrelates faster for a given velocity.

dials.name: sliderAngle
dials.origEffect: Full 360deg rotation of the rain direction over 0..1: v=0 falls DOWN (+y), v=0.25 moves LEFT (-x), v=0.5 moves UP (-y), v=0.75 moves RIGHT (+x), v=1 wraps back to DOWN. Measured on 48x48 as +/-10 px per 0.1 s along the expected axis at each setting.
dials.portEffect: Identical mapping and identical directions at all four cardinal settings (+/-4 px per 0.1 s on 48x48, i.e. same signs, ~2.5x smaller magnitude). Angle is the port's best-ported dial. NOTE: on the 16x16 rig the port's directions read as REVERSED — that is an aliasing artefact of its ~2.3-row texture period, not a real sign error; confirmed on 48x48.

dials.name: sliderScale
dials.origEffect: Zoom/drop-size. v=0 gives many thin streaks; v=0.5 medium; v=1 gives 1-2 very wide fat streaks filling much of the canvas. Feature count falls and width grows monotonically.
dials.portEffect: Same direction — v=0 gives a dense field of small square blobs, v=0.5 the default dash texture, v=1 a single column of wide horizontal bars. Magnitude/direction fine; the glyph is wrong at every setting (horizontal bars/blobs rather than vertical streaks).

dials.name: sliderLightning
dials.origEffect: Strike frequency. v=0 = no lightning at all (max whole-grid mean brightness 9 over 120 s); v=0.5 = 12 strikes / 120 s (mean gap 10.3 s); v=1 = 23 strikes / 120 s (mean gap 5.4 s). Peak flash brightness constant at 101 regardless of setting.
dials.portEffect: Same shape (v=0 correctly disables lightning entirely, max 9) but ~4.3x too frequent everywhere: v=0.5 = 54 strikes / 120 s (mean gap 2.2 s), v=1 = 97 strikes / 120 s (mean gap 1.2 s). Peak flash brightness 122 vs the original's 101, and strikes often fire 4-5 sub-flickers where the original fires 1-2.

feedback: Rewrite the raindrop glyph. The original draws each drop as a THIN LINE ALONG ITS DIRECTION OF TRAVEL: at sliderAngle=0 a ~1-2 px wide, 8-25 px long vertical streak with a saturated head that fades along the trailing tail. The port draws a segment PERPENDICULAR to travel — a 2-px-tall, 2-8 px wide horizontal dash. Whatever axis the port is elongating the drop on, it is the wrong one; the streak must be extruded along the motion vector, not across it.

Make the rain sparse and randomly placed, on true black. Original: 39% of pixels non-zero at lightning=0, 27% above value 8, and every unlit pixel is exactly 0,0,0 with only 1-2 dominant spatial features per canvas height (row-profile DFT k=1). Port: 69% non-zero, 45% above 8, no pixel ever reaches 0, and a strong k=5-7 periodic texture. Drop up the periodic tiling and drive drop positions from independent random x/phase per drop; remove whatever constant ambient term is keeping the whole grid at value 1-15.

Drop x-positions must not be quantised to fixed columns. With lightning off, the port's per-column mean is constant to within cross-correlation c=0.999 over 120 s — columns 4 and 5 are permanently ~25x brighter than columns 0-3. The original's column profile drifts continuously. Whatever hashes the drop x-coordinate is aliasing onto a handful of grid columns.

Speed up the base fall rate ~4.5x. At angle=0, lightning=0, speed/scale untouched, the original travels ~3.8 canvas-heights per second (60 rows/s on 16x16, ~190 px/s on 48x48); the port travels ~0.83 canvas-heights per second (0.32 rows/frame at 40 fps on 16x16, 40 px/s on 48x48). The sliderSpeed response curve has the right shape, so this is a constant multiplier on the base velocity, not a dial-mapping bug.

Cut the lightning rate by ~4x. Target the original's cadence: at sliderLightning=0.5 about one strike every 10 s, at 1.0 about one every 5.4 s, and never more than 1-2 sub-flickers of 0.05-0.10 s per strike. The port currently fires every 2.2 s / 1.2 s respectively and produces bursts of 4-5 sub-flickers. sliderLightning=0 correctly disables lightning on both sides, so only the rate constant is wrong.

Trim the flash amplitude/radius slightly. At peak, the original's whole-grid mean is 94.6 with 96% of pixels lit; the port's is 121.4 with 100% lit. Both peak at 255 in the core, so shrink the glow radius (or steepen its falloff) rather than lowering the core brightness.

Fix the drop colour. Original drop heads are [12,12,254] — R and G exactly equal, i.e. pure blue with a small white desaturation. Port heads are [20,26,161] — cyan-shifted (G ~30% above R) and only ~63% as bright. Raise the drop head to saturate near 254 and make the desaturation channel-neutral.
sliderAngle, sliderSpeed and sliderScale are all mapped correctly (angle in particular is exact: 0=down, 0.25=left, 0.5=up, 0.75=right, 1=down). Do not touch their mappings while fixing the above.
